bibliography.title: High-accuracy sampling for diffusion models and log-concave distributions

abstract_sentences.text: We present algorithms for diffusion model sampling which obtain δ-error in polylog(1/δ) steps, given access to eO(δ)-accurate score estimates in L2.
This is an exponential improvement over all previous results.
Specifically, under minimal data assumptions, the complexity is eO(d⋆ polylog(1/δ)) where d⋆ is the intrinsic dimension of the data.
Further, under a non-uniform L-Lipschitz condition, the complexity reduces to eO(L polylog(1/δ)).
Our approach also yields the first polylog(1/δ) complexity sampler for general log-concave distributions using only gradient evaluations.

final_judgment.single_storyline: The paper replaces unavailable density-value rejection sampling with bounded unbiased gradient-based tilt corrections, makes that primitive FORS, and reuses it for reverse diffusion kernels and RGO. [pp. 5–8, §§3–4, explicit: “simulate rejection sampling”; p. 12, §5, explicit: “RGO is exactly a Gaussian tilt”]
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The main text keeps the access-model gap, all three algorithms, the d⋆ definition, the headline theorem statements, representative log-concave consequences, and the no-experiment boundary. [pp. 5–12, explicit: “FORS guarantee”; p. 12, explicit: “left for future work”]
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Proofs, tail/coverage tools, the one-step Gaussian KL characterization, detailed concurrent comparison, and the formal log-concave theorem move to A–G; theorem verification therefore requires the appendix. [pp. 16–43, layout observation: “Appendix”; p. 43, explicit: “Proof … is therefore omitted”]
final_judgment.best_pattern: A one-dimensional Bernoulli-factory derivation precedes Algorithm 1, then the same Gaussian-tilt primitive is threaded into diffusion and RGO; the ordering exposes the mechanism before the headline rate. [pp. 5–7, interpretation grounded in “We motivate our approach” and “General path integral”]
final_judgment.largest_gap: The paper offers no implementation or empirical evaluation, and the log-concave extension assumes exact proximal points while omitting a proof; cross-work rate comparison is textual rather than a common benchmark. [p. 12, explicit: “future work”; p. 42, explicit: “assume that this error is zero”; p. 16, explicit: “In comparison with our results”]
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For a new theoretical capability, derive a reusable primitive on a minimal toy problem, state its exact interface guarantee, then replace one local link in the existing end-to-end chain and sum the propagated errors. [pp. 5–9, interpretation grounded in Eq. (8), Algorithm 1, and Theorem 4.3]
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: The rule needs application-level control of the primitive’s assumptions: here bounded/clipped estimators, early stopping, score-error norm, non-uniform Lipschitz conditions, and an exact or accurate proximal solve remain essential. [pp. 7, 9–11, 21–23, 42, explicit: “Assumption 3.2”; “Assumption 4.8”; “assume … zero”]
